questions.q: What is the special term used to describe why your right hand appears as your left hand in a mirror?
questions.a: The term is "lateral inversion." Answering incorrectly often suggests the student confuses this with "reflection" or "inversion" (turning upside down), revealing they haven't distinguished between vertical flipping and horizontal swapping.

questions.q: If you stand 2 metres in front of a plane mirror, how far behind the mirror does your image appear to be?
questions.a: It appears 2 metres behind the mirror. A wrong answer (like "0 metres" or "4 metres") shows the student does not understand that the image distance behind the mirror matches the object distance in front.

questions.q: You write the word "SCIENCE" on a piece of paper and hold it up to a plane mirror. What will the word look like in the reflection?
questions.a: It will appear as a laterally inverted reflection where the letters are reversed (ECNEICS). If the student writes it normally, they have failed to apply the property of lateral inversion to physical objects.

questions.q: Why is an image formed by a plane mirror called a "virtual" image?
questions.a: It is called virtual because it cannot be projected onto a screen; it only appears to exist behind the mirror. Answering "because it is fake" is partially correct but misses the technical requirement that it cannot be captured on a surface.

questions.q: If an object is 5 cm tall, how tall will its image be in a plane mirror?
questions.a: The image will be 5 cm tall. Answering "larger" or "smaller" suggests a misunderstanding of the "same size" property, likely influenced by experiences with magnifying glasses or distant objects.

questions.q: Design a simple test to prove that an image in a plane mirror is at the same distance behind the mirror as the object is in front.
questions.a: Place a pencil 10 cm from the mirror, then place a second pencil behind the mirror at the position where the image appears; if the second pencil matches the image's location, it proves the equal distance. Poor answers describe only looking at the image without providing a way to measure or verify the position behind the mirror.
